name: arpeggio-neck
description:
A chord's arpeggio in one box on the guitar neck, or across two neighbouring boxes with the notes they share marked as
the seam; show only part of it, say which notes are in play (`enable`) and which of them stand out (`highlight`).
Tap a note to hear it, play the box up and down.

props.name: chord
props.description: the chord: "Am", "G7", "Cmaj7"

props.name: boxes
props.description: one box, or two neighbouring boxes (1-based, as numbered in the arpeggio cues): [2] or [2, 3]; absent shows box 1

props.name: placement
props.description:
where on the neck, instead of `boxes`: { "by": "open" } next to open chords, { "by": "root", "string": 6 } the box
with the root on the low E (5: the A string, 4: the D string), { "by": "fret", "fret": 7 }, { "by": "chords" } near the
chords shown in this exercise, { "by": "box", "box": 2 }; use `boxes` only when the exercise is about the boxes

props.name: part
props.description: only these degrees of the chord (major-relative to the chord root): ["1","b3"]

props.name: enable
props.description: the notes in play: degrees (major-relative, from the chord root) or note names: ["1","3"] or ["c-sharp"]; the rest are muted (see `others`). Absent: every note

props.name: highlight
props.description: the notes of interest, ringed: the roots, the one new note, the note that differs; they stay playable. Never the same list as `enable`

props.name: mute
props.description: notes drawn faint, same forms as `enable`

props.name: hide
props.description: notes not drawn, same forms as `enable`

props.name: others
props.description: the notes not in `enable`: "muted" (default) or "hidden"

props.name: show
roots
props.description: with `show`: the strings the root is shown on, 2 to 6 (6 is the low E): [6, 5]; absent: all of them

name: arpeggio-part
description:
Part of an arpeggio (for example 1-3, or 1-3-5) over a chord or a progression; chords cycle to fill `bars`, the
degrees repeat one per beat. `place` gives each chord a box and part; `across` connects one arpeggio from one box
part to the next. Only some neighbouring box pairs share notes (for example Am box 2 upper and box 3 lower), so
crossings work best between boxes that overlap. `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "arpeggio-part", "chords": ["C","Am","F","G"], "degrees": ["1","3","5"], "bars": 4, "place": [{ "box": 1, "part": "lower" }, { "box": 1, "part": "upper" }, { "box": 2, "part": "lower" }, { "box": 2, "part": "upper" }] }`

props.name: key
props.description: optional key as a note ("c")

props.name: chords
props.description: chord names: "C", "Am7"

props.name: degrees
props.description: arpeggio degrees from the chord root: ["1","3","5"]

props.name: across
props.description: cross from one box part to another: { "from": { "box": 1, "part": "upper" }, "to": { "box": 2, "part": "upper" } }

props.name: place
props.description: box and part per chord, in order

props.name: bars
props.description: total bars

props.name: guide
props.description: cue text per step, in order

name: backing-band
description:
A metronome, a drone on the key's root, drums and bass to play or listen along with, in a key at a tempo; each part offered
gets a switch. `parts` says which are offered and how each starts.
Example: `{ "type": "backing-band", "bpm": 70, "key": "a", "parts": { "click": "on" } }` is a plain metronome.
Example: `{ "type": "backing-band", "bpm": 60, "key": "e", "parts": { "drone": "always", "click": "off" } }` keeps the drone
sounding and lets the student add the click.

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 30-240

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: parts
props.description:
the parts offered, "click", "drone", "drums", "bass", each with how it starts: "on" (playing, the student can switch it
off), "off" (silent, the student can switch it on), "always" (playing, no switching it off). A part left out is not there

name: backing-track
description:
A backing track to play or sing over: drums, bass and keys playing a chord progression in a style, looping until
stopped. It shows the chords as boxes (the one playing lit) and a mixer, so the student can mute a part
to play it themselves. The student can change the progression, key, style and tempo. Use it to improvise or comp over a
whole band (a 12-bar blues shuffle, a minor vamp, a jazz ii-V-I), and under a singer singing over chords (guide tones,
chord notes, a line of their own, next to a staff with the mic). Give a curated `progression`, or the lesson's own
chords as `chords` or `numerals`, one per bar. For hearing a progression on the guitar's own shapes use
guitar-play-along; for a beat or a drone without chords, backing-band.

Example: `{ "type": "backing-track", "progression": "blues", "key": "a", "style": "shuffle", "bpm": 90 }` plays a
12-bar blues in A as a shuffle: A7 D7 A7 A7 D7 D7 A7 A7 E7 D7 A7 E7.
Example: `{ "type": "backing-track", "key": "d", "numerals": ["I", "IV", "V", "I"], "style": "ballad", "parts": { "drums": "on", "bass": "off", "keys": "always" }, "bpm": 70 }`
plays D G A D on piano and soft drums under a singer; the piano can't be muted, the bass can be added.
Example: `{ "type": "backing-track", "progression": "pop", "key": "g", "parts": { "drums": "always", "bass": "on" } }` leaves
the keys out, so the student plays the chords themselves over drums and bass.

props.name: progression
props.description: the progression, by id. Major: "pop" (I V vi IV), "fifties" (I vi IV V), "three-chord" (I I IV V), "canon" (I V vi iii IV I IV V), "ii-v-i" (ii7 V7 Imaj7 Imaj7), "turnaround" (Imaj7 vi7 ii7 V7), "blues" (12-bar: I7 IV7 I7 I7 IV7 IV7 I7 I7 V7 IV7 I7 V7), "bossa" (Imaj7 Imaj7 ii7 V7), "waltz" (I IV V7 I, 3/4), "reggae" (I IV). Minor: "andalusian" (i bVII bVI V), "minor-pop" (i bVI bIII bVII), "minor-ii-v" (iiø7 V7 i7 i7), "minor-blues" (12-bar: i7 iv7 i7 i7 iv7 iv7 i7 i7 bVI7 V7 i7 V7), "aeolian" (i bVI bVII i). Modes: "dorian" (i7 IV7), "phrygian" (i bII), "lydian" (Imaj7 II), "mixolydian" (I bVII IV I)

props.name: chords
props.description: instead of `progression`: the chords in order, one per bar, looping, up to 16; repeat a chord to hold it longer: ["D", "D", "A", "A"]

props.name: numerals
props.description: instead of `progression`: numerals counted on the major scale of `key`, one per bar, up to 16 (I ii iii IV V vi vii°, i for minor, V7, ii7, bVII, iiø7)

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note, the I (or the i of a minor or modal progression): "a" with "minor-blues" is A minor; "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat". With `chords` it may be left out: the first chord's root

props.name: style
props.description: how the band plays it (default: the progression's own, "ballad" for chords of the lesson's own): "pop", "rock", "ballad", "swing", "shuffle", "bossa", "funk", "reggae", "waltz" (3/4)

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 40-220 (default: the style's usual tempo)

props.name: parts
props.description:
the parts offered, "drums", "bass", "keys", each with how it starts: "on" (playing, the student can mute it), "off" (muted,
the student can unmute it), "always" (playing, no mute). A part left out is not played and has no row. Absent: all three
"on". A singer often wants the bass "off"; a student comping the chords leaves "keys" out

name: breathwork
description:
A breathing exercise for singers, no mic and no instrument: a circle that grows as the student breathes in, stays
while they hold and shrinks as they breathe out, the count ticking in the middle, a soft tick on each count and a
chime when the phase changes (no spoken voice). A strip under it shows every phase to come. Drills: "farinelli"
(breathe in, hold and breathe out for the same count, one count more each cycle), "sss-zzz" and "zzz-sss" (a hiss,
then the same with voice, to feel where the voice starts), "cycles" (in, hold, out, rest), "long-exhale" (in for 4,
out slowly for longer) and "body-scan" (breathe into the belly, the ribs, the back).

props.name: level
props.description: farinelli only: how hard, in one word; it sets `from` and `to` where you leave them out: "new" 2 to 5, "beginner" 3 to 8, "intermediate" 4 to 10, "advanced" 4 to 20

props.name: drill
props.description: "farinelli" (default), "sss-zzz", "zzz-sss", "cycles", "long-exhale" or "body-scan"

props.name: from
props.description: farinelli only: the first count, 2-12; default 4 (a beginner 2 or 3)

props.name: to
props.description: farinelli only: the last count, from `from` up to 20; default 8 (a beginner 8, intermediate 10, advanced 20). Each count is one second, so 4 to 8 takes about 1.5 minutes

props.name: seconds
props.description: the drill's main length in seconds, 2-16: each sss and zzz (default 3), each in, hold and out of "cycles" (default 4), the breath out of "long-exhale" (default 8, the breath in is always 4), each part of "body-scan" (default 8). Not for farinelli

props.name: rounds
props.description: rounds, 1-8: sss-zzz and zzz-sss default 3, cycles and long-exhale 4, body-scan 2. Not for farinelli

name: caged-neck
description: The CAGED shapes of the key's chord on the guitar neck (the minor shapes when the scale has a minor 3rd): with `shapes`, those shapes one under another, each with its chord, arpeggio, pentatonic and scale; without, all five on the whole neck. Use it for how the five shapes join up the neck.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

props.name: shapes
props.description: the shapes to show, from "C", "A", "G", "E", "D"; absent: all five on the whole neck

name: chord-circle
description: One chord of the key in the middle, with its sus and extended chords around it (sus2, sus4, add9, 7th, 9th); tap one to hear it. Use it to show what a chord can turn into while it still fits the key.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

props.name: degree
props.description: the chord in the middle: the note of the scale it is built on, 1 to 7 (1 is the key's own chord); absent: 1

name: chord-shapes
description:
One chord diagram per chord, in order, with the finger that frets each note on its dot (a switch shows intervals
instead); tap a diagram to strum it. Show a fingering with this, never describe it in text.

props.name: chords
props.description: chord names in order: ["G", "Em", "C", "D7"]

props.name: voicing
props.description: "open" (default, the easy shape) or "barre" (the movable barre shape, lowest on the neck)

name: chord-steps
description:
Per chord, a list of steps, one beat each: "strum", a degree, or a grip (notes struck together on chosen strings: a
triad, a double stop). Mix them to make a riff: two notes, a triad, two notes, a double stop. Each chord takes one bar,
more when its steps need them. Degrees are major-relative semitones from the chord root (default) or the key (when `key` is given). `guide`
gives a cue per step, in order. `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "chord-steps", "voicing": "barre", "chords": [{ "chord": "G", "steps": ["strum","1","6","1"] }, { "chord": "D", "steps": ["strum","4","5","4"] }] }`
Riff: `{ "shape": "chord-steps", "chords": [{ "chord": "G", "steps": ["5","3",{ "grip": ["1","3","5"], "strings": "321" },{ "grip": ["3","5"], "strings": "21" }] }] }`

props.name: key
props.description: optional key ("g"); needed for degreesFrom "key"

props.name: chords
props.type: { chord: string; steps: ("strum" | Degree | Grip)[]; place?: Place }[]
props.description: chords in order, each with its steps and optional box/part

props.name: degreesFrom
props.description: "chord" (default) or "key"

props.name: voicing
props.description: "open" (default) or "barre"

props.name: guide
props.description: cue text per step, in order; missing ones get a default cue on a box change

name: circle-of-fifths
description: The circle of fifths, majors outside and their relative minors inside, with the key's neighbours marked: the keys next to it are the chords of the key. Tapping a key on the circle moves the panel there. Use it for how keys are related and why some keys share most of their chords.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: finger-pattern
description:
A finger-pattern drill: the spider and finger permutations,
one finger per fret, played on each string in turn. Use it for dexterity and finger independence warm-ups.

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets `fingers` and `fret` where you leave them out: "new" 1234 from fret 5 (the frets are closer there), "beginner" 1234 from fret 1, "intermediate" 1324, "advanced" 1423. The tempo is yours to set: a faster `bpm` is the next step inside a level

props.name: fingers
props.description: the fretting fingers in playing order, 2-4 different digits 1-4: "1234" (the spider), "1324", "13"; needed unless `level` is set

props.name: fret
props.description: the fret under finger 1, 1-12; default 1

props.name: strings
props.description: the strings to play, 1-6 (6 = low E); default all six

props.name: show
props.description: the row under the tab: "finger" (the fretting finger, for beginners) or "pick" (the pick stroke ↓ ↑); unset, the student switches between them, starting on finger

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 40-200; default 80

name: guitar-play-along
description:
Play along on the guitar with a click and piano: the music shown as tab, as note names or on the neck, all following
one clock. For the guitar only: a singer singing over chords gets a backing-track instead.
You choose the musical content as a shape; the app computes the notes, frets, strings and timing. Shapes, by name:
`progression`, `two-scales`, `chord-steps`, `arpeggio-part`, `melody`, `solo-over` (see each shape's doc).
The student can change tempo and view, and pick a backing when the shape offers more than one. Under single-note
steps over chords (guide tones, arpeggio parts) the app holds each chord softly by default, so the student hears the
harmony and not just the click; `under` changes that.

Example: `{ "type": "guitar-play-along", "shape": { "shape": "chord-steps", "voicing": "barre", "chords": [{ "chord": "G", "steps": ["strum","1","6","1"] }, { "chord": "D", "steps": ["strum","4","5","4"] }] }, "bpm": 70 }`

props.name: shape
props.description: the musical content: one shape object, its `shape` field naming it

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 30-240

props.name: view
props.description: first view: "tab" (default), "notes" or "neck"

props.name: enable
props.description: the degrees the student plays (major-relative, from the chord root): ["1","3","5"]; the rest are muted (see `others`). Absent: every note

props.name: highlight
props.description: the degrees of interest among those, ringed on the neck: ["1"]; never the same list as `enable`

props.name: others
props.description: the notes not in `enable`: "muted" (default) or "hidden"

props.name: under
props.description: what sounds under the steps besides the click when the shape has no comping `backing`: "chords" (each chord held; the default when the steps are single notes over chords), "drone" (the key's root held; the shape's key, else the first chord's root) or "none"

name: improvisation
description: Ideas to improvise with in the key: a rhythm made from two counts against each other, and one short motive turned round, written in the key's notes. Use it to give a student something to make up lines from, next to a backing-track or a drone.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: interval-ears
description: An ear-training game: hear an interval or chord and name it.

props.name: kind
props.description: "interval" (default) or "chord"

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, for kind "interval": which intervals are asked, each level adding to the ones before. A number 1-6: 1 the 5th and octave, 2 adds the 3rds, 3 the 4th and major 2nd, 4 the minor 2nd and the 6ths, 5 the 7ths and the tritone, 6 all twelve. Or a word: "new" is 1, "beginner" 2, "intermediate" 4, "advanced" 6. `set` replaces it. The next step inside a level: `dir` "down", then "together", then `wide`

props.name: set
props.description: the interval sizes in semitones to ask: [3,4,7]

props.name: dir
props.description: direction: "up", "down" or "together"

props.name: wide
props.description: intervals may span more than an octave

name: interval-singer
description:
Sing a given interval from Do: the interval shows by name ("Interval · P5 · Do ↑ Sol"), Do sounds and sits on a piano
roll (or a staff, the student's switch), and the student sings the other note with the microphone; held on it, it
counts, shows and plays back. With `play` "both", Do and then the note sound, so the student copies the leap. Restart (or Space) plays Do again for the interval asked; Skip moves on. Once it is
sung, Next (or Space) asks another interval from the set, in another key when there are several, and R restarts it. Tapping Do or the "?" plays that note. The voice shows as a dot unless `dot` is false (the harder way: no
picture of the voice, only whether it counted). A singing exercise.

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets `intervals`, `dir` and `keys` where you leave them out. "new": major 3rd and 5th up, the home chord [4, 7]. "beginner": adds the octave [4, 7, 12]. "intermediate": the leaps of the major scale, 4th, 5th, major 6th, octave [5, 7, 9, 12]. "advanced": the leaps that are hard to hear, minor 3rd, tritone, minor 6th, minor 7th, major 7th [3, 6, 8, 10, 11], up and down, Do in a random key each time. The next step inside a level: `dir` "down" then "both", more `keys`, then `dot` false

props.name: key
props.description: the key: Do's note name, e.g. "c", "f#", "bb"; default "c". "random": any of the 12, a new Do each question

props.name: keys
props.description: several keys to pick Do from at random, a new one each question: ["c", "g", "f"]; or "random" for all 12. The student can change them on the tool

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range; default "tenor"

props.name: intervals
props.description: the intervals to ask, in semitones from Do (1 to 12): [7] only the 5th, [4, 7, 12] (the default) the major 3rd, 5th and octave

props.name: dir
props.description: "up" (default): above Do; "down": below Do; "both"

props.name: play
props.description: what sounds before the student sings: "do" (the default), only Do, so the student finds the note; "both", the easier way for a new singer: Do and then the note to sing, so the student hears the leap and sings it back

props.name: dot
props.description: show the voice as a dot; default true. false is the harder level: sing without seeing the voice

props.name: picker
props.description: show the Keys switch and the twelve key chips on the tool, so the student picks the keys; default false: the keys are the ones set here, and a choice with `key` options on the section is how the student changes key

name: key-chords
description: The chord on every note of the scale, with its numeral; tap a chord to hear it. Use it for the chords of a key as a set; triads for one chord's shapes on the guitar.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: legato-trill
description:
A legato trill: two fingers on one string, alternating by
hammer-on and pull-off with no picking after the first note. Use it for legato strength and finger independence.

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets `fingers` where you leave them out, the strong pair first: "new" 12, "beginner" 13, "intermediate" 23, "advanced" 34 (the two weakest fingers). The tempo is yours to set: a faster `bpm` is the next step inside a level

props.name: fingers
props.description: the two fingers, lower one first, two different digits 1-4: "12", "13", "24"; needed unless `level` is set

props.name: string
props.description: the string, 1-6 (6 = low E)

props.name: fret
props.description: the fret under the first finger, 1-12

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 40-200; default 80

name: lip-roll
description:
A lip roll warm-up with the mic: a soft tone slides from head voice down to chest voice (or back up, or holds one
note) while a line shows its path over the voice's registers, and the student lip rolls it while the mic draws their
line over it: with the tone, then on their own (the default), with the tone only, or with no tone (`play`). Each round
goes a little deeper into chest voice (one note: a semitone lower), then a short rest; `plays` rounds in all. The
slide crosses both breaks of the voice type (typical ones, `REGISTERS`), so it smooths the change from head to chest
voice. The line is loose on purpose: a lip roll is about an easy, steady buzz, not an exact note. A singing warm-up,
for the start of a voice session.

props.name: shape
props.description: the path: "down" (default; from head voice to chest voice), "up" (chest to head voice), "siren" (up and back down) or "hold" (one steady chest-voice note)

props.name: speed
props.description: how fast the tone slides: "slow", "medium" (default) or "fast"; the student can change it on the tool. Not for "hold"

props.name: play
props.description: when the tone plays: "echo" (default; a pass with the tone, then the same pass on your own, its first note sounding and fading as you start), "always" (the tone the whole time, lip rolled with) or "silent" (no tone, only the line); the student can change it on the tool

props.name: seconds
props.description: "hold" only: how long the note lasts, 2-10 seconds; default 5

props.name: plays
props.description: how many rounds, 1-8; default 3

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range; default "tenor"

name: melody
description:
A tune from the singing book, by number, in a key. `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "melody", "tune": 3, "key": "d" }`

props.name: tune
props.description: melody book number (1-based)

props.name: key
props.description: key as a note: "c", "f-sharp"

name: melody-singer
description:
A tune from the singing page's melody book on a staff, in a key and voice: play it to hear it, tap a note, then sing
it with the microphone along a bar that runs over the tune. Pick the tune from `melodyChoices()` (one per stage).

props.name: tune
props.description: the tune's number in the melody book (a number, from melodyChoices); omit it and give `pick` instead

props.name: pick
props.type: { difficulty?: string; stage?: string; index?: number }
props.description: choose the tune by what it is like instead of by number: difficulty (easy, medium, hard, expert), a stage id and which of the matches (index from 0)

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note (Do): "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range; default "soprano"

props.name: chords
props.description: the piano's chords under the tune, one a bar, named over the staff; in a run, the two chords in the held-Do bar that announce each new key. Default true; false for the tune alone

props.name: metronome
props.description: the metronome heard from the start, on the tune's beats (beat 1 of each bar accented); default false. The student can switch it, the tune and the chords on and off in the player either way

name: mode-intervals
description: The notes of the key on one panel: spelled, numbered from the root and coloured by degree, with the step pattern and what the mode is used for. Use it beside a scale-neck to show what sets a mode apart (the ♭3 of Dorian, the ♯4 of Lydian).

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: note-finder
description: A game to find notes on the fretboard: find a named note, play every note, or name the note shown.

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets the strings, the frets and the notes asked. "new": the low E and A strings, frets 0-5, natural notes only. "beginner": the same two strings up to fret 12. "intermediate": all six strings, frets 0-12, sharps and flats too. "advanced": all six strings up to fret 15. The next step inside a level: `mode` "name"

props.name: mode
props.description: "find" (default), "every" or "name"

props.name: strings
props.description: which strings, as digits low to high: "123456" (default all)

props.name: from
props.description: first fret of the range, 0-24

props.name: to
props.description: last fret of the range, 0-24

name: piano-keys
description: A piano keyboard with the key's notes marked in their degree colours; tap a key to hear it. Use it to show a scale's notes laid out in a row, apart from the guitar.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: picking-drill
description:
A picking-hand drill: a stroke pattern repeated across the
strings. Use it for alternate picking (strokes "DU") and, with skip, for string skipping.

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets `strokes`, `notesPerString` and `skip` where you leave them out: "new" all downstrokes, four notes a string; "beginner" down-up, four notes a string; "intermediate" down-up, three notes a string (each string starts on the other stroke); "advanced" down-up, two notes a string, skipping a string. The tempo is yours to set: a faster `bpm` is the next step inside a level

props.name: strokes
props.description: the pick strokes in order, 1-8 of D (down) and U (up): "DU", "DDU"; needed unless `level` is set

props.name: notesPerString
props.description: notes picked on each string before moving on, 1-4; default 4

props.name: strings
props.description: the strings to play, 1-6 (6 = low E); default all six

props.name: skip
props.description: jump over a string each time instead of moving to the next one; default false

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 40-200; default 80

name: position-neck
description:
The scale on the whole guitar neck, drawn across: only the positions asked for are framed and playable, every other note
is faint. A row of position thumbnails under the neck lets the student pick others. With `cross` it shows just the way
from one position to the next: the lower position's notes on the low strings, both on the crossing string (the slide),
the upper position's on the high strings; the rest of both positions is faint. Use it for positions on the neck and
for joining them; `scale-neck` for one position studied on its own.

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "minor-pentatonic", "dorian", "major-ionian"

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: kind
props.description: "3nps" for the scale's seven 3-notes-per-string positions, one framed at a time (`positions` holds one, 1 to 7; no `cross`, no `placement`); absent: the scale's own five positions

props.name: positions
props.description: the positions framed (1-based, 1 to 5; with `kind` "3nps", one of 1 to 7); absent: position 1, or the two in `cross`

props.name: placement
props.description: where on the neck, instead of `positions`, as on `scale-neck`: { "by": "root", "string": 5 } frames the position with the root on the A string

props.name: cross
props.type: { from: number; to: number; string?: number }
props.description:
show only the way across between two positions: { "from": 1, "to": 2 }; `string` is where it crosses, numbered 1 to 6
(6 is the low E), default 3 (the G string)

props.name: add
props.description: notes from outside the scale to play too, as note names: ["e-flat"]; they are highlighted

props.name: enable
props.description: the notes in play inside the framed positions: degrees or note names, as on `scale-neck`; the rest are muted. Absent: every note

props.name: highlight
props.description: the notes of interest, ringed: the roots, the crossing notes. Never the same list as `enable`

props.name: mute
props.description: notes drawn faint, same forms as `enable`

props.name: hide
props.description: notes not drawn, same forms as `enable`

props.name: others
props.description: the notes not in `enable`: "muted" (default) or "hidden"

props.name: outside
props.description: the notes outside the framed positions (or the crossing): "muted" (default, drawn faint) or "hidden"

props.name: picker
props.description: the thumbnails and crossing buttons under the neck; false fixes the view to what the exercise sets

name: progression
description:
A chord progression, by chord names or by numerals in a key, cycled to fill `bars`. Optional `steps` repeat over
each chord's beats, one beat each ("strum", a degree or a grip). Degrees are major-relative semitones ("3" is always 4),
counted from the chord root (`degreesFrom: "chord"`, default) or the key. `backing` lists comping patterns, the
first plays first. `place` gives each chord a box and part, in order. `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "progression", "key": "g", "numerals": ["I","IV","V"], "steps": ["1","3","5"], "bars": 4 }`

props.name: key
props.description: key as a note: "g", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: numerals
props.description: I ii iii IV V vi vii°, bVII, V7 (major-key degrees; lower case = minor)

props.name: chords
props.description: chord names, used when numerals are absent: "G", "Em7"

props.name: bars
props.description: total bars; chords cycle to fill them

props.name: beatsPerChord
props.description: beats per chord (2, 3 or 4), default 4; in 4/4, 3 lets chords start mid-bar (beats 0, 3, 6, 9...)

props.name: steps
props.description: repeated step template: "strum", a degree like "1", "b3", or a grip: { "grip": ["1","3","5"], "strings": "321" }

props.name: degreesFrom
props.description: what the step degrees count from: "chord" (default) or "key"

props.name: voicing
props.description: "open" (default) or "barre"

props.name: backing
props.description: comping patterns the student can pick, first one plays first

props.name: place
props.description: box and part per chord, in order: [{ "box": 1, "part": "lower" }]

name: progressions
description: Common chord progressions that suit the key's mode, written as chords in the key; tap one to hear it. Use it to show which progressions a mode is heard in, not to play along (backing-track does that).

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: relative-modes
description: The modes that share the key's notes, each starting from another note of the scale. Tap one to see the same notes from its own root. Use it to show that a mode is the key's notes heard from a new home note; it has nothing to play along with.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: run-singer
description:
A run from the singing page's runs book on a staff, moving up a semitone each pass, across a voice: its last pass tops
out on the voice's highest note, so the keys come from the voice, not picked. Play it, then sing it with the microphone. Pick the run from `runChoices()` (one per stage).

props.name: run
props.description: the run's number in the runs book (a number, from runChoices); omit it and give `pick` instead

props.name: pick
props.type: { difficulty?: string; stage?: string; index?: number }
props.description: choose the run by what it is like instead of by number: difficulty (easy, medium, hard, expert), a stage id and which of the matches (index from 0)

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range; default "soprano"

props.name: chords
props.description: the piano's chords under the tune, one a bar, named over the staff; in a run, the two chords in the held-Do bar that announce each new key. Default true; false for the tune alone

props.name: metronome
props.description: the metronome heard from the start, on the tune's beats (beat 1 of each bar accented); default false. The student can switch it, the tune and the chords on and off in the player either way

name: scale-neck
description:
The scale's positions (boxes) on the guitar neck; tap a note to hear it, play a box up and down. Pick which boxes
to show, add notes from outside the scale, say which notes are in play (`enable`) and which of them stand out
(`highlight`).

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "natural-minor-aeolian", "minor-pentatonic"

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: boxes
props.description: which boxes to show (1-based); absent shows all

props.name: parts
props.description:
what is drawn, as on a backing-band: "positions" (the boxes) and "neck" (the whole neck lying flat, above them, with
the shown position framed on it and the same notes in play), each "on" (shown, the student can hide it), "off"
(hidden, the student can show it) or "always" (shown, no switch); a part left out is not drawn. Absent: the boxes
alone. { "positions": "always", "neck": "on" } when the exercise is about where a position sits on the neck or how
it moves with the key; { "neck": "always" } for the whole neck alone

props.name: neck
props.description: older, the studio's Scale widget: true shows the scales page's whole neck above the boxes, without `enable` or `highlight`; exercises use `parts`

props.name: positions
props.description: older, with `neck`: false hides the boxes

props.name: placement
props.description:
where on the neck, instead of `boxes`: { "by": "open" } next to open chords, { "by": "root", "string": 6 } the box
with the root on the low E (5: the A string, 4: the D string), { "by": "fret", "fret": 7 }, { "by": "chords" } near the
chords shown in this exercise, { "by": "box", "box": 2 }; use `boxes` only when the exercise is about the boxes

props.name: add
props.description: notes from outside the scale to play too, as note names: ["e-flat"] (the blue note, say); they are highlighted

props.name: enable
props.description: the notes in play: degrees (major-relative, from the key root, not scale-aware) or note names as in `add`: ["1","b3"] or ["c-sharp"]; the rest are muted (see `others`). Absent: every note

props.name: highlight
props.description: the notes of interest, ringed: the roots, the one new note, the note that differs; they stay playable. Never the same list as `enable`

props.name: mute
props.description: notes drawn faint, same forms as `enable`

props.name: hide
props.description: notes not drawn, same forms as `enable`

props.name: others
props.description: the notes not in `enable`: "muted" (default) or "hidden"

props.name: chords
props.description:
chords of the key to find inside the shown positions, as numerals of the key: ["i","iv","♭VII"] (case and ♭ don't
matter, the key decides the chord). A chip each; pressing one rings that triad wherever the position holds it on
`chordStrings` (the rest faded) and strums it. A chord the positions don't hold there gets no chip: a pentatonic
position lacks two notes of its key, so use the full scale ("natural-minor-aeolian", "major-ionian") for every chord.
For seeing the chords inside a scale, before soloing over them

props.name: chordStrings
props.description: the three strings the chords sit on, as guitar numbers: "321" (default: G, B, high e), "432", "543", "654"

name: solo-over
description:
Improvise over chords. The code comps the chords (bass + chord by default). The neck shows one fixed set of notes for
the whole progression: the exercise's `scale` (from `key`) plus every chord's own `scale` (from the chord root), or
the chord tones when no scale is given. Nothing moves but the highlight: the sounding chord's `target` degrees
(major-relative, from the chord root), also named above the neck ("land on B"), with the optional `approach` hint.
A chord's `stab` is a grip the student strikes on its beat 1 before improvising (a triad from the position on
`"321"`), lit on the neck while the chord sounds: chords and a solo in one hand position.
No fixed notes, nothing graded. Each chord takes `bars` bars (default 1). `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "solo-over", "key": "a", "scale": "minor-pentatonic", "chords": [{ "chord": "Am7", "target": ["1"] }, { "chord": "D7", "target": ["3"], "approach": "land on F♯ on beat 1" }] }`

props.name: key
props.description: key as a note: "g"

props.name: scale
props.description: the scale improvised in, from `key`, for the whole progression: "minor-pentatonic", "dorian"

props.name: chords
props.type: { chord: string; scale?: string; target: Degree[]; approach?: string; stab?: Grip }[]
props.description: chords in order with an optional extra scale slug (from the chord root), target degrees, optional hint and stab: { "grip": ["1","b3","5"], "strings": "321", "fret": 5 }

props.name: bars
props.description: bars per chord, default 1

props.name: backing
props.description: comping pattern for the backing

name: staff
description:
The scale on a staff in a voice's range, with the microphone's pitch drawn on it; tap a note to hear it. With `drone` and/or
`click` it carries its own backing, so a singing exercise needs no `backing-band` beside it: starting the mic also starts the drone,
the drone UI provides start/stop and mute controls, and the step's "Start exercise" starts both together (Stop exercise stops both).

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "minor-pentatonic"

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range: "bass", "baritone", "tenor", "alto", "mezzo", "soprano"

props.name: notes
props.description: only these degrees are on the staff (major-relative): ["1","3","5","b7"]; absent shows the whole scale

props.name: under
props.description: also the staff's notes under the lowest Do, down to the voice's lowest note, so a line can dip to Ti under Do; default false

props.name: enable
props.description: the notes in play: degrees (major-relative, from the key root, not scale-aware) or note names: ["1","5"] or ["c-sharp"]; the rest are muted (see `others`). Absent: every note

props.name: highlight
props.description: the notes of interest, ringed (the enabled rest stay plain, the muted faint): the root, the one new note; never the same list as `enable`

props.name: mute
props.description: notes drawn faint, same forms as `enable`

props.name: hide
props.description: notes not drawn, same forms as `enable`

props.name: others
props.description: the notes not in `enable`: "muted" (default) or "hidden"

props.name: mic
props.description: show the "Start microphone" button; default true

props.name: drone
props.description: a drone on the key's root under the singing, with its own Play; the step's "Start exercise" starts it and the mic together; default false

props.name: click
props.description: a metronome click under the singing, played like `drone` (with the drone when both are set); default false

props.name: bpm
props.description: the click's tempo, 30-240; default 60

props.name: labels
props.description: the label under each note: "degree" (1 2 3) or "solfege" (Do Re Mi). Absent: the student's setting, and with the mic never bare note names (degrees then)

name: string-singer
description:
Sing the guitar's open strings to learn their pitches for tuning by ear, on a staff with the microphone, at the
guitar's own pitch (E2 to E4): play it to hear the notes, tap one, then sing along a bar. Three drills: the strings one by one,
neighbouring pairs (the intervals a guitar is tuned by), and the 5th-fret unisons (the lower string's 5th fret, the
4th on G, is the next open string).

props.name: level
props.description: how hard, in one word; it sets `drill` where you leave it out: "new" and "beginner" the strings one by one, "intermediate" the pairs, "advanced" the 5th-fret unisons

props.name: drill
props.description: "strings" (default): E A D G B E up and back down; "pairs": each two neighbouring strings, low then high (fourths, a major third G to B); "fifth-fret": the lower string's 5th fret then the next open string, the same note

props.name: metronome
props.description: the metronome heard from the start; default true (it keeps the long notes in time). The student can switch it and the tune on and off in the player either way

name: strum-along
description:
Strumming practice: a metronome and the chords as a row of boxes, one per bar (or per beat), the box playing lit.
Each chord box holds its beats and each beat its strums, the strum due now lit. One bar of count-in clicks first, then
the boxes loop until the student stops. Use it whenever the student strums chords in time; give the strum as
`pattern` ("D . D U . U D U") rather than only in the text. For hearing a progression played by the app, use a play-along.

Example: `{ "type": "strum-along", "chords": ["Em", "Bm"], "bpm": 70, "pattern": "D . D U . U D U" }` shows
[ Em  [↓ ·][↓ ↑][· ↑][↓ ↑] ] | [ Bm  [↓ ·][↓ ↑][· ↑][↓ ↑] ]

props.name: chords
props.description: the chords in order, one per block, looping; repeat a chord to hold it longer: ["Em", "Em", "Am", "Am"]

props.name: bpm
props.description: tempo, 30-240

props.name: per
props.description: how long each block lasts: "bar" (default) or "beat" (a chord change on any beat; fill whole bars)

props.name: beats
props.description: beats in a bar, 2-6; default 4

props.name: pattern
props.description:
one bar of strokes, the same every bar: D down, U up, . a miss (the hand moves, no strings); 1-4 strokes a beat, the
same count in every beat, so beats × 1, 2, 3 or 4 strokes. "D D D D" downs on the beat, "D U D U D U D U" eighths,
"D . D U . U D U" the island strum, "D . . U . U D U D . . U . U D U" sixteenths; default a down on every beat

name: triads
description: One chord of the key as a triad in its three inversions on one group of three strings; the student picks the chord and the string group on the tool. Use it for triad shapes on the guitar; key-chords for the chords of a key as a set.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: tunings
description: An instrument's tuning, string by string, with the open strings that are notes of the key lit, since they ring freely in it; the student picks the instrument and the tuning on the tool. Use it for open and alternate tunings.

props.name: key
props.description: the key's root note: "c", "f-sharp", "b-flat"

props.name: scale
props.description: scale slug, e.g. "major-ionian", "dorian", "natural-minor-aeolian"; a pentatonic or blues slug is drawn in the major or minor scale it comes from

name: two-scales
description:
Play in one scale, then switch to another at a bar (default halfway), same click throughout. Each side has its own
key. The backing chord is comped underneath (without one, a drone on the first key). The neck shows both scales'
notes the whole time: the backing chord's tones highlighted, the notes outside the scale playing now muted, so the
switch shows as the changed note. `bpm` goes on the play-along.

Example: `{ "shape": "two-scales", "a": { "key": "a", "scale": "minor-pentatonic" }, "b": { "key": "a", "scale": "dorian" }, "bars": 8 }`

props.name: a
props.description: first scale: key ("a") and scale slug ("minor-pentatonic", "dorian", "major-ionian")

props.name: b
props.description: second scale, same form

props.name: bars
props.description: total bars, at least 2

props.name: switchBar
props.description: bar the switch happens at (0-based), default half of bars, kept within 1..bars-1

props.name: backingChord
props.description: optional chord comped underneath: "Am"

props.name: backing
props.description: comping pattern for the backing chord, default "bass-chord"

name: video
description:
A practice video from the app's video library, played with the browser's own controls: play, pause, the time bar, full screen.
The student plays or sings along with it. No mic. Pick the video by its id from the list below; write how long it runs into the
exercise's time.

props.name: video
props.description: the video's id in the library (a string from the list)

props.name: ref
props.type: { source: string; id?: string; title?: string; text?: string }
props.description: notes only, never in a plan: a teacher's recording or a placeholder ({ "source": "recording", "id", "title" } or { "source": "placeholder", "text" }) in place of `video`

name: voice-hill
description:
A warm-up for the voice with the mic: the student holds one easy sound (a hum, "oo" or "ee") in one part of their
voice while a ball on a hill shows it. "low": the ball rolls down into the hollow as the voice goes low; "high": it
climbs to the top as the voice goes up, light and easy; "middle": it rests in a valley between two marks. Held there,
a ring fills over `seconds`; each full ring is one hold, then a breath, `reps` holds in all. Off the place, sung, the
ring drains slowly; a breath pauses it. Play note sounds the note at the place's edge. No key and no notes to read.
A singing exercise, for a warm-up or for finding the low and the light high voice.

props.name: where
props.description: where in the voice: "low" (default; the bottom of the voice: each hold a semitone lower, a tenor's E3 and under down to C3 and under, the new note played in the breath between), "middle" (a few notes over it, a tenor's F3 to B♭3) or "high" (head voice, over the second break: a tenor's G4 and over; keep it light)

props.name: sound
props.description: the sound to hold: "hum" (default), "oo" or "ee". "oo" suits the low and the high voice, a hum any place

props.name: seconds
props.description: how long each hold lasts, 2-10 seconds; default 3

props.name: reps
props.description: how many holds, 1-8; default 5

props.name: voice
props.description: voice range; default "tenor"
